question.text: This president, the first one from the Democratic Party, sought to destroy the Second Bank of the United States by vetoing its recharter bill.
question.clue: This man hung two British citizens in the Arbuthnot-Ambrister affair, and he was the victor at the Battle of Horseshoe Bend.

swap.text: Marshall was a member of this political party that advocated for a strong central government.
swap.clue: The Coodies were a faction of this party from Maryland.

question.leadin: The Election of 1824 was a mess.
question.text: The eventual winner, John Quincy Adams, was said to have entered a "corrupt bargain" with this man, who finished fourth in the election and became Secretary of State.
question.clue: This man resolved an electoral college deadlock in what became known as the "Corrupt Bargain".

swap.leadin: This court case established the concept of judicial review.
swap.text: Name this court case where John Adams appointed the plaintiff to the position of federal justice of the peace in a midnight appointment, but Jefferson did not deliver the appointment.
swap.answerHtml: Marbury v. Madison [or Madison v. Marbury; prompt on partial answer as neither name is uniquely identifying by itself]
swap.clue: This case decided it was "emphatically the province and duty of the judicial department" to deny to issue a writ of mandamus to the plaintiff, who was appointed as a Justice of the Peace.

question.leadin: This battle's namesake mission in San Antonio was defended by such men as Davy Crockett.
question.text: Name this battle in which Mexican soldiers slaughtered the defending Texans, led by Colonel Travis.
question.clue: This battle is said to have caused the "Runaway Scrape" along with the Goliad Massacre.

swap.text: This man's brother Tenskwatawa led the Native American forces at the Battle of Tippecanoe. Later, this Shawnee leader was killed by Richard Mentor Johnson at the Battle of the Thames during his war.
swap.clue: Trained in early life by Joseph Brant, he led a small force to Vincennes to discuss the earlier Treaty of Fort Wayne; afterwards he traveled southward to gain support from the Five Civilized Tribes.

question.text: The earthquakes may have been felt as far away as Washington, D.C., where this president was preparing for the War of 1812. This shortest president drafted the Bill of Rights and succeeded Thomas Jefferson.
question.clue: In another essay, this politician wrote that "Ambition must be made to counteract ambition," and "If men were angels, no government would be necessary."

swap.leadin: This nation won the battle of San Jacinto in under twenty minutes.
swap.text: Name this short-lived country which was eventually annexed as a U.S. state. It used the battle cry "Remember the Alamo!" while breaking free of Mexico.
swap.clue: After a week of drinking, a leading candidate for the presidency of this nation, James Collinsworth, drowned during its 1838 election which was won by a man who introduced the "redback" currency, Mirabeau Lamar (MERE-uh-bow luh-MAR).

question.text: This president, who essentially failed to respond to Dorr's Rebellion, is also famous for rebelling against the Whigs after succeeding William Henry Harrison.
question.clue: His Secretary of State was one of the few to remain loyal to him, possibly because he was negotiating an end to the Aroostook War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the suffrage movement, per part.
swap.text: This Founding Father, who had an extensive correspondence with his wife, vowed that men would fight "the despotism of the petticoat."
swap.answerHtml: John Adams [prompt on Adams, do not accept John Quincy Adams]
swap.clue: This man engaged in the Quasi War with France, following the XYZ Affair.

question.text: This man, who was later killed at York in the War of 1812, was imprisoned in Santa Fe in 1806 during the same river exploration mission that discovered a certain mountain in the Front Range. His report on Santa Fe spurred American interest in the Texas territory.
question.clue: He died leading an expedition against modern day Toronto in the War of 1812.

swap.leadin: The first of these conflicts began when a flag pole in front of the American consulate in Tripoli was chopped down.
swap.text: Give the collective names for these two conflicts, sometimes dubbed the Algerian and Tripolitan wars, fought between the United States and several North African States.
swap.answerHtml: Barbary Wars [accept Barbary Coast Wars or Barbary Pirates Wars]
swap.clue: During the first of these wars, Stephen Decatur led a daring raid on the enemy-controlled USS Philadelphia and burned it.

question.text: The events of the Panic of 1907 included the collapse of New York's third-largest trust, which was named after this word. A satirical 1809 history popularized this term for New Yorkers who had Dutch ancestry.
question.answerHtml: knickerbocker [accept Knickerbocker's History of New York; accept Dietrich Knickerbocker; accept Knickerbocker Trust Company]
question.clue: A character of this surname was held to have gone missing before the publication of an 1809 "history" that popularized his baggy-kneed pants.

swap.leadin: This agreement limited military capacity on the Great Lakes and Lake Champlain to two vessels for each of the signing powers.
swap.text: Name this agreement between the United States and Britain that was signed in the wake of the War of 1812.
swap.clue: The Webster-Ashburton treaty built on this 1818 agreement which curtailed the use of naval boats on the Great Lakes and set much of the US-Canada border at the 49th parallel.

question.leadin: This case implied that Native Americans did not have complete rights to their land, such as Georgia claiming the Yazoo lands.
question.text: Name this 1810 case that found that a state had no authority to void contracts.
question.clue: This 1810 case of the Marshall Court is cited as the first time the Supreme Court struck down a state law as unconstitutional. This case involved land speculators on Yazoo tribal lands in Georgia.

swap.leadin: The only indentured servant ever to serve in Congress, Matthew Lyon, was the first person convicted under this act.
swap.text: Name this act. Samuel Chase and James Callendar threatened to beat and kill each other after Chase imprisoned Callender under this act.
swap.clue: While circuit riding, Samuel Chase drew the ire of Republicans for presiding over the prosecution of many Republicans under this law. James Callender was jailed under this law.

question.leadin: A form of this concept is compared to the agoge system in Sparta in an essay stating that John Locke's First Treatise of Government integrated women into social theory.
question.text: Name this concept. Intellectual historian Linda Kerber introduced the "republican" type of this concept, which claims that post-independence women were encouraged to educate themselves to maintain morality.
question.answerHtml: republican motherhood [prompt on answers describing women in the domestic sphere]
question.clue: This patriotic ideal of the Revolutionary era, according to which the role of women is to instill the namesake patriotic values in their children.

swap.leadin: This speech claimed that almost ninety thousand dollars had been spent by Democrats on the White House since they had taken control of the presidency.
swap.text: Name this speech by Charles Ogle that lambasted Martin Van Buren's spending habits. This speech takes its name from a piece of cutlery.
swap.clue: This speech delivered over three surreal days to the House of Representatives, the same year that Democrats refused to re-nominate Richard Mentor Johnson.

question.leadin: Archibald Cox promoted the theory that George Washington created the precedent of executive privilege in the aftermath of this military disaster.
question.text: What battle prompted the first congressional investigation into the executive branch? The US's first standing army was formed after this "defeat," at which Little Turtle destroyed an expedition led by its namesake officer.
question.answerHtml: St. Clair’s (“Sinclair’s”) defeat [or Battle of the Wabash River; or Battle of a Thousand Slain]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about some shady business dealings.
swap.text: This was the name given to the 1795 sale of vast holdings in a certain river valley by the Georgia legislature to four companies following the wholesale bribery of the legislators.
swap.clue: Several companies at the center of this scandal were offshoots of the Combined Society.
